ConocoPhillips edged up just under 0.5% today to $133.19, but the stock is still down 2.9% over the past two weeks—a decline that tracks closely with the falling oil prices that have dominated this week. Oil fell sharply on news that Saudi Arabia is releasing additional crude supplies to offset disruptions from Houthi strikes, easing the market's fear of a prolonged shortage; U.S. crude is trading at $107 per barrel, well below the $130+ range seen earlier in the period. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly cut into profits on the barrels it produces, which is why the stock has drifted lower despite today's modest bounce.

The sharp reversal on Tuesday—a $4.55 jump from $136.67 to $141.22—suggests briefly heightened concern about supply disruptions in the Middle East, but that optimism reversed hard on Wednesday when the Saudi supply news hit. With geopolitical tensions still high but supplies stabilizing, crude prices are unlikely to spike higher anytime soon, keeping downward pressure on exploration and production companies in the near term.
